result.title: RAPID: Codec-Aware Video Decoding for Efficient Long-Video Understanding
result.summary: Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can process hour-long videos, but the large number of input frames incurs substantial inference overhead. Existing approaches to efficient long-video understanding largely overlook video decoding, which can take longer than LLM prefill. We propose RAPID (Reference- and Access-Point-Informed Decoding), a codec-aware framework that exploits information embedded in compressed bitstreams to reduce both frame decoding and selection costs. RAPID consists of two components. RAPID-Dec exploits reference-frame information and random access points to skip unnecessary frames and decode the retained frames in parallel while preserving exact reconstruction of the target frames. It achieves up to a 3.7x decoding speedup over the fastest baseline on H.264/AVC videos. RAPID-Sel uses keyframes as coarse representatives of video segments, avoiding the dense candidate decoding and scoring required by existing frame selection methods. It achieves comparable accuracy with up to a 3.0x preprocessing speedup. Together, RAPID achieves a 4.9x time to first token (TTFT) speedup on hour-long videos over a state-of-the-art frame selection method using the fastest baseline decoder.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 codec-aware 框架 RAPID：利用压缩码流中的参考帧与随机访问点信息跳过不必要帧并并行解码目标帧，并用关键帧作为片段粗代表避免帧选择时的密集解码与打分，从而降低长视频 VLM 的解码与预处理开销、提升 TTFT。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「低成本粗代表预筛 + 跳过密集候选」的做法可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与计算预算分配提供线索，并给出证据获取成本的可核查量化；但工作停留在输入解码层，不涉及 latent 推理状态或模型内部信息使用。
